description: Negative financial and operational language in SEC filings — impairments, defaults, losses, and deterioration indicators. Structured for merge with user-supplied custom dictionaries.

entries.note: Auditor doubt about company ability to continue as a going concern — severe signal
Significant deficiency in internal controls — SEC reportable, audit risk
Correction of previously filed financial statements — integrity risk
Recognized write-down of asset value — non-cash but signals deterioration
Write-down of acquired business value — often large and material
Asset write-down — signals declining asset value
Reduction of carrying value on balance sheet — reduces reported assets
Full removal of asset value from balance sheet — 100% impairment
Failure to meet debt obligations — may trigger acceleration of debt
Breach of debt agreement covenants — may trigger default
Period with negative earnings — company not profitable
Core business generating negative income from operations
Historical losses exceeding retained earnings — persistent unprofitability
Cash outflows exceeding inflows in the period — liquidity concern
Explicit statement of operational or financial constraint
Negative impact stated on operations, financial condition, or results
Negative impact on business metrics or financial condition
Negative variance or condition relative to expectations or prior period
Worsening of financial or operational condition over time
Material downward movement in a key financial or operating metric
Weakening customer or market demand — revenue risk indicator
Loss of existing customers — revenue and growth risk
Worsening conditions in the company addressable market
Risk of loss from counterparty non-payment or credit deterioration
Risk of inability to meet short-term financial obligations
Failure to fulfill contractual obligations — legal and financial exposure
End of material agreement, relationship, or employment
Non-recurring cost from reorganization — signals operational disruption
Explicit statement of revenue reduction — financial deterioration signal
Explicit characterization of a risk as material and significant
